titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 15, the hymns (part 2 of 4)
part: Spell 15 — the hymns, part 2 of 4: a litany of greetings to Osiris and a hymn to Ra at his rising in the eastern horizon (Plates 19–20)
work: Book of the Dead of Ani
workEn: Book of the Dead of Ani
draftNote: Draft — the hieroglyphs are read from the printed type of Budge's 1895 edition of the papyrus, and the signs and readings are still being checked; expect changes.
source: Papyrus of Ani (British Museum EA 10470), Plates XIX, XX. Hieroglyphs transcribed from the interlinear text of E. A. W. Budge, The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum (London, 1895), pp. 127–131; Budge's transliteration and word-by-word English were used to check the reading of the signs and the sense, never for wording. Only the papyrus's own text is given: the passages Budge supplies from other papyri in his appendixes and footnotes are left out. Transliteration in the Leiden convention, with the reed written i; translation made fresh from the Egyptian. Shown left to right; the papyrus is written in columns read from the top down. The line under each word ("say") is the conventional Egyptological classroom pronunciation — a neutral e between consonants; ꜣ and ꜥ as a; w as u or w; ṯ as tj; ḏ as dj; ḫ and ẖ as kh; š as sh — an artificial teaching pronunciation, since the vowels of Egyptian were never written. The grouping of signs within a word follows Budge's type, which regularises the scribe's hand.
about: The second part of Spell 15 begins on Plate 19 with a litany: ten short strophes, the first nine opening with the greeting 'hail to you' written in red, that hail Osiris by his names and his cities (Heliopolis, Busiris, Heracleopolis, Abydos, Nekhen) and end with Ani asking for a way to pass in peace. On Plate 20 a new hymn begins, to Ra as he rises in the eastern horizon: Ani asks that his ba may travel with the sun in its two barks, and then greets the sun as Horakhty and Khepri, the god whom those in the Duat come out to see. It ends as Ani says he has come to the land of eternity, and the hymn runs on into the next part. Budge's type is uncertain in several signs, and the notes say where a reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · the-stars · in · Heliopolis(?) · the-Henmemet · in · Kher-aha(?)
sentences.i: Hail to you, (you of) the stars in Heliopolis(?) and of the Henmemet in Kher-aha(?)!
sentences.n: The litany of Spell 15 begins: ten strophes, the first nine opening with ind ḥr·k 'hail to you', which the papyrus writes in red (Budge's line numerals 1 to 10 mark them, one line to a strophe). ind is the reed i and a post with a knobbed top (the sign nḏ, Aa27, approximate), here without the papyrus roll; ḥr·k is the face ḥr with its stroke and the basket ·k: literally 'greetings to your face', as in the first part of the spell. Budge prints ànet' and ḥrà-k as two groups, and they stay two words. ḫꜣbsw 'stars' is a sign coded M12, the lotus ḫꜣ (in the print a stalk with a curled top on a flared base, approximate; Q7 does not fit; M12 writes ḫꜣ in Spell 1 as well), read ḫꜣ with Budge, ꜣ as complement, foot b, the folded cloth s, the star as classifier and plural strokes; the reading of the first sign is doubtful. m iwnw: the pillar iwn stands alone (O28, approximate), perhaps a short writing of iwnw 'Heliopolis', which is spelled in full at the end of the strophe; Budge leaves it as Àn. ḥnmmt 'the Henmemet' is the disk with hanging rays (N8), the owl m twice, t and plural strokes: beings of the sun's light. ḫr-ꜥḥꜣ is the butcher's block ḫr (T28, approximate), a rounded stela (O26, approximate), a low sign with marks (N29, approximate) and the town sign; Budge reads χer-āba. It is taken, doubtfully, as Kher-aha, the district by Heliopolis named in Spell 125 (written there ḫ-r-ꜥ-ḥ-ꜣ); here only ḫr and the town sign are clear: neither the stela nor the low sign has a value that spells ꜥḥꜣ, and the stela is coded as carrying it only because the reading needs a place for it. No 'lord of' is written: Budge supplies '[lord of] … [and of]'; the vocative is kept as it stands, and the English supplies only '(you of)' to make the relation readable.

sentences.i: Wenty, more effective than the hidden gods who are in(?) Heliopolis!
sentences.n: wnty 'Wenty' (Budge: Unti) is the hare wn with water n as complement, t, two strokes y and the seated god: a god's name, perhaps 'he who exists' from wnn 'be'. Budge supplies '[thou]'. ꜣḫ r nṯrw 'more effective than the gods': the adjective ꜣḫ 'effective, glorious' (Budge: 'glorious more') (the crested ibis ꜣḫ, ḫ as complement; the chick w after it, Budge's χu, is not read, then a tall sign with ticks, Y1a, and a stroke) followed by r 'than', the way Egyptian makes a comparison. nṯrw is the flag written three times. štꜣ 'hidden' is the long hatched rectangle š (N37, approximate), a flat sign with grains taken as tꜣ (N16, approximate), a small cup (W10, approximate; taken as a classifier) and ꜣ, with the crossed sticks and a flat sign with a tuft (Aa13, approximate) as classifiers: the adjective after nṯrw, its plural ending unwritten. imyt is Z11 im with m and t: the nisba 'who is in', but feminine where 'the gods' would want imyw; it may be the preposition imytw 'among' (Budge: àmt, as in the first part of the spell), and the form is doubtful. iwnw 'Heliopolis' is the pillar, the pot nw and the town sign.

sentences.i: Hail to you, Pillar in Iun-des(?), Horus in the two horizons, wide of stride as he crosses the sky!
sentences.n: Strophe 2; ind ḥr·k in red as before. iwn 'Pillar' is the pillar (O28, approximate) with a stroke, three small strokes and the seated god: a name of the god, as in the hymn to Osiris (Budge: Àn). iwn-ds is the pillar again with a knife lying across (coded T30, read ds with Budge, approximate) over a low sign with a wavy top (N25, approximate); Budge reads Àn-ṭes with a (?) in his English, and the place is not known. ḥr 'Horus' is the falcon with r and the seated god. ꜣḫty 'the two horizons' is the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ, t, two strokes y and two dotted oblongs as classifiers (N18, approximate; no horizon sign N27 is printed): the dual of ꜣḫt, the horizons of sunrise and sunset. pd nmtt 'wide of stride': p, a bar with turned-down ends (coded N1, approximate; perhaps the bow pḏ, which writes this word elsewhere in the papyrus), the hand d and the walking legs, then nmtt 'stride', the legs with t and a stroke; Budge prints peṭ and nemmat, and the legs after the hand are taken with pd. ḏꜣ·f ḥrt 'he crosses the sky': ḏꜣ is a tall tapering sign (the fire-drill ḏꜣ, U28, approximate) with ꜣ and a boat as classifier (P1, approximate), a sḏm·f with ·f; ḥrt is the face, r, t and the sky. The god is the sun striding across heaven.

sentences.i: Hail to you, this ba of eternity, the ba who is in Busiris, Wennefer, son of Nut!
sentences.n: Strophe 3; ind ḥr·k in red. bꜣ 'ba' is the ram (E10), the ba-sign of the ram of Mendes, with a small incense bowl before it (R7, the house practice) and a stroke. pw 'this' (p and the chick w) is the demonstrative after its noun; n ḥḥ 'of eternity' is the genitive n and the wick ḥ twice with the sun-disk between as classifier, the n of nḥḥ unwritten as in the first part of the spell. The second bꜣ is the ram with its stroke, two reeds and the seated god (Budge: Bai, 'Ram-god'); the two reeds are not read, and may make the word bꜣy. imy ḏdw 'who is in Busiris': imy is Z11 im with m and two strokes y; ḏdw 'Busiris' (Djedu) is the djed-pillar twice, w and the town sign. wnn-nfr 'Wennefer', 'he who is (always) perfect', is the hare wn with water twice, the heart-and-windpipe nfr and the seated god. sꜣ nwt 'son of Nut': the pintail duck sꜣ with its stroke, and nwt written with the pot nw, t and the sky, with a cobra on a basket (I13, approximate) as classifier. The ba of Osiris was held to rest in Busiris, his city in the Delta.

sentences.n: Plate 20 begins a new hymn, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes dwꜣw and ḫft wbn·f in red, Ra and the rest of the title in black. dwꜣw 'adoration' is the hand d and a looped cord taken as wꜣ (V4, approximate), ꜣ, the star dwꜣ as classifier, ꜣ again, the chick w, a man raising both arms (approximated) and the roll, as at the opening of the hymn to Osiris in the first part; Budge prints ṭua-ṭuau. rꜥ 'Ra' is r and U15 for ꜥ, with the seated god wearing the sun-disk. ḫft wbn·f 'when he rises': ḫft 'in front of, at the time of' is the placenta ḫ, the viper f and t, and before a verb it means 'when'. ꜣḫt iꜣbtt nt pt 'the eastern horizon of the sky': ꜣḫt is the sun between hills with t and a house-like sign; iꜣbtt 'eastern' is the emblem of the East with b, t twice and the hill-country sign; nt is the genitive in the feminine, agreeing with ꜣḫt; pt 'sky' is p, t and the sky. ḥꜥ n imyw-ḫt·f: Budge prints ḥā en as one group, and it is split here into ḥꜥ 'rejoicing' (the wick ḥ and U15 for ꜥ, with no classifier) and the genitive n; Budge takes ḥꜥ as a verb, 'rejoice those who …', and either reading is possible. imyw-ḫt 'those in the following' is Z11 im, w and a stroke, the sign ḫt (M3) with ḫ and t, the seated god and a stroke, and ·f; Budge's numeral 2 is printed inside the word.

sentences.i: may he proceed in the Mandjet-bark, may he moor in the Sektet-bark, may he mingle among the Unwearying Stars in the sky.
sentences.n: Three wishes in the sḏm·f, each with ·f, 'he', the ba. wḏꜣ·f 'may he proceed' is a thin staff with a looped head (coded V24, wḏ, approximate), the chick w and the walking legs; Budge reads utu-f, 'may he go forth'. It is read wḏꜣ 'proceed', as in the same wish in the first part of the spell (wḏꜣ·k, there with the fire-drill ḏꜣ, a similar tall sign); the ꜣ is not written. mꜥnḏt 'the Mandjet-bark', the bark of the morning, is the owl m with the arm ꜥ joined to it, a sign of two crossing curves taken as the netting needle ꜥnḏ (V26, approximate), the hand d, t twice and a boat (P1, approximate); the first part of the spell has the shorter name ꜥḏt with the same sign. mni·f 'may he moor' is the gaming board mn with n, the reed, a mooring post (P11, approximate) and a boat; sktt 'the Sektet-bark', the bark of the evening, is s, k, t twice and a boat. ꜣbḫ·f 'may he mingle' is the emblem of the East (R15, iꜣb) used for its sounds ꜣb, with b as complement, the placenta ḫ, the crossed sticks and a kneeling man carrying a load (A9, approximate) as classifiers, and ·f: ꜣbḫ 'mix, mingle, join with', said of the dead joining the stars; the i of the sign is not read (Budge: àbeχ-f, 'may he go'). iḫmw-wrd 'the Unwearying Stars' is the reed i, ḫ, Aa15 m, the negative arms and plural strokes, then the swallow wr with r, the hand d, a slumped figure (A7, approximate) and the star with plural strokes; Budge's numeral 6 stands inside the word. They are the stars that never cease moving.

sentences.n: nbt-wnwt 'the Lady of the Hour' is the basket nb with t, then wnwt 'hour', the hare wn with n, the pot nw and t, with a cobra (I12) as classifier: a goddess, here the uraeus serpent on the sun's head. mn·ṯi 'established' is the gaming board mn with n, then a tall hooked sign (coded V13, approximate and doubtful) and the papyrus roll as classifiers, and the ending ·ṯi (the rope ṯ and the reed): the stative of the 3rd person feminine, after its subject. m tp·k 'on your head'. šmꜥt·s 'her southern one' is the tall stem šmꜥ (M26, approximate) crossed at its foot by U15 for ꜥ, t, a tilted oval (coded H8, approximate) and a cobra as classifiers, and the bolt ·s; Budge reads qemāt-s, his old value for the sign. mḥt·s 'her northern one' is the papyrus clump mḥ (M16, approximate) with t, the same two classifiers and ·s. sentences.n: Two passives in the sḏm·tw·f, each negated by n (the negative arms D35, approximate, with water n as complement), with no subject written, Ani understood: '(I) have not been shut in, (I) have not been turned back' (n with the sḏm·f, here in its passive, denies a past act, as in the last strophe of the litany); Budge supplies '[I]' and renders as a wish, 'may [I] not be'. ḫni·tw is the placenta ḫ, water n, the reed, a face in profile (D19) and U15 as classifiers, and the tw (t and w) of the passive: the verb ḫnr 'restrain, shut in', written without its r as elsewhere in the papyrus (Budge: χenà-tu). šnꜥ·tw is the cord šn (V7, approximate) with n, U15 for ꜥ, a lying lion (E23, approximate; it may be the forearm D40) and the walking legs, and tw: šnꜥ 'turn back, repel'; the lion rw is written in this verb in Spell 1 as well and is not read (Budge: śenār-tu). Budge's numeral 13 stands between the two clauses.

sentences.i: My limbs are renewed at the sight of your beauty, like all your favoured ones,
sentences.n: mꜣw 'are renewed' is the sickle mꜣ with ꜣ, two small strokes, the chick w and the papyrus roll (Budge: maiu): the sḏm·f of mꜣwi 'be new, be renewed', with its subject ḥꜥw·i 'my limbs' (ḥ, U15 for ꜥ, a fleshy curl, F51 approximate, plural strokes and ·i). m dgꜣ nfrw·k 'in the seeing of your beauty': dgꜣ 'see, look at' is a long rounded sign (coded X4, approximate) over a stand (coded Q7, approximate), ꜣ and the eye as classifier; the two upper signs are read d and g, and the shapes are not certain: the long sign is coded X4 as in dgg 'look' in the introduction to Spell 18, and the stand coded Q7 has no value g, which belongs to the jar-stand W11 it may be. Budge prints ṭeka with an undotted k (his k is k), but dgi 'look at', spelled here with ꜣ, is the word the eye classifier calls for. nfrw·k 'your beauty' is nfr with a stroke and plural strokes, the abstract plural, and ·k. mi ḥsyw·k nbw 'like all your favoured ones': mi is the milk-jug in its net (W19, approximate) with the reed; ḥsyw is the wick ḥ, a tall jar ḥs (W14, approximate), the bolt s, two reeds y and a man with his hand at his face, the plural of the passive participle 'favoured', with ·k; nbw 'all' (Budge's numeral 14 follows).

sentences.i: for I am one of those whom you honoured on earth.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes a sun-disk before the genitive n; read n. ḥr ntt 'because': the preposition ḥr with ntt 'that', the conjunction made from the relative nty, introducing a clause; Budge glosses the pair together. ink wꜥ m 'I am one of'. nn 'these, those' is water n, the adze nw (U19, approximate), the pot nw and w (Budge: ennu): the demonstrative before its noun, joined to it by the genitive n. The genitive n after it is printed with a small ring with a dot (the sun-disk N5) before the water-line; the ring has no sense here, and Budge too reads only en. šps·n·k 'whom you have honoured' is a noble seated on a chair (A51, approximate), the bolt s twice, the roll, a stroke, water n and ·k (Budge: śepses-nek): taken as the relative sḏm·n·f of šps 'be noble', used of making someone noble, honouring him; only one s is read, and the verb in this use is not certain. tp tꜣ 'upon earth': tp, the head, as a preposition, and the land sign tꜣ. The favoured of the god on earth are those he favours in death.

sentences.i: I have reached the land of eternity, I have joined the land of everlastingness.
sentences.n: iw opens the statement. pḥ·n·i 'I have reached' is the hindquarters of a lion pḥ (F22, approximate) with the walking legs, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i (Budge prints peḥ-nà as one group and renders 'may I arrive'). r tꜣ n ḥḥ 'to the land of eternity': ḥḥ again without its first n. ḫnm·n is the jug ḫnm with m, the roll and the n of the sḏm·n·f; no ·i is printed after it (Budge: χnem-nà, '[may I] be united'), and the 'I' is understood from the clause before. Budge's numeral 15 is printed inside the word, between the roll and the n. r tꜣ n ḏt 'to the land of everlastingness': ḏt is the cobra curling round t over the land sign with grains (N16, approximate). The two lands are one: the realm of time without end.

sentences.i: It is you, indeed, who ordained it for me, my lord.
sentences.n: ntk is wḏ n·i st: ntk 'you' with a participle after it, 'it is you who …', strengthened by is 'indeed' (the reed and the folded cloth s, drawn upright). wḏ 'who ordained' is the staff with a coiled top wḏ (V24, approximate) with w as complement and the roll: the participle of wḏ 'command, decree'. Budge prints utu-nà as one group; it is split here into wḏ and n·i 'for me' (water n and the seated man). st 'it' is the dependent pronoun (the bolt s and t), the object. nb·i 'my lord' is the basket nb with a seated long-wigged figure as classifier and ·i. The hymn goes on in the next part with 'O Osiris Ani …'.

glossary.n: n — not; negates the verb ('I have not …') · also in n wn "there is not" · a second word of the same spelling: the preposition "to, for" (n·i "to me") · the negative also before a noun, 'without, there being no …' · the preposition also 'because of, on account of'
glossary.ḥꜥw: ḥꜥw — limbs, body, flesh (noun m. plural)
glossary.tꜣ-ḏsr: tꜣ-ḏsr — 'the Sacred Land', the cemetery, realm of Osiris (place name m.; tꜣ 'land' + ḏsr 'holy'; Budge: Ta-sert)
glossary.bwt: bwt — abomination, what is taboo, what one detests (noun f.)
glossary.grg: grg — to speak falsehood, tell lies · also lies, falsehood (noun; ḏd grg 'speak lies') · a second word of the same spelling: to found, establish (verb)
glossary.ḥry-ib: ḥry-ib — middle, midst (noun; lit. "what is upon the heart"; m ḥry-ib "in the midst of") · also the inside, inner parts (of the body) · also who is in the midst of, who dwells in (nisba epithet after a noun or name; nṯr ꜥꜣ ḥry-ib ꜣbḏw 'the great god who dwells in Abydos')
glossary.wiꜣ: wiꜣ — boat, bark, especially of a god (noun)
glossary.ini: ini — to bring, fetch (verb 3ae-inf.; sḏm·n·f in·n·i 'I have brought')
glossary.ḥꜥpy: ḥꜥpy — Hapy, the Inundation, the Nile flood as a god (god's name, noun m.; Budge: Ḥāpi)
glossary.tpḥt: tpḥt — cavern, hollow, hole in the earth (noun f.; plural tpḥwt)
glossary.wbn: wbn — to rise, shine forth (verb; of the sun)
glossary.šw: šw — empty, lacking, free (of) (adjective; verb šwi 'be empty') · a second word of the same spelling: Shu, god of the air, who holds up the sky (god's name; Budge: Śu) · a third word of the same spelling: sunlight, light (noun m.; written with the feather šw and the sun as classifier)
glossary.nḫn: nḫn — child, infant (noun; plural nḫnw) · a second word of the same spelling: Nekhen, Hierakonpolis, the old city of Horus in Upper Egypt (place name; Budge: Neχen)
glossary.nswt-bity: nswt-bity — king of Upper and Lower Egypt (title; lit. 'he of the sedge and the bee')
glossary.wsir: wsir — Osiris, god of the dead and king of the world below; Wsir N "the Osiris N", the dead person (god's name; Budge: Àusàr)
glossary.mꜣꜥ-ḫrw: mꜣꜥ-ḫrw — true of voice, vindicated (epithet; said of the dead whose words were found true at the judgement) · also, as a noun, vindication, the being found true (m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'in vindication'; written in full or short)
glossary.tꜣ: tꜣ — to be hot; tꜣ-ib 'hot-tempered' · a second word of the same spelling: land, earth (noun; plural tꜣw 'lands'; dual tꜣwy 'the Two Lands', Egypt; tp tꜣ 'upon earth')
glossary.sp: sp — time, occasion; deed, case, matter (noun); sp sn 'twice'
glossary.mnḫ: mnḫ — effective, excellent, beneficent (adjective; plural mnḫw)
glossary.idbwy: idbwy — the Two Banks, Egypt on either side of the river (dual noun, from idb 'bank'; Budge: àṭeb)
glossary.·i: ·i — I, me (1st-person singular suffix pronoun; the seated-man sign)
glossary.swꜣ: swꜣ — to pass, pass by (verb; swꜣ ḥr 'pass by'; written with the crossed sticks and walking legs)
glossary.ink: ink — I (1st person singular independent pronoun; ink N "I am N")
glossary.ꜥqꜣ: ꜥqꜣ — straight, exact (adjective; Budge: āqa, 'the middle') · also as a noun, straightness, exactness (?)
glossary.ḏd: ḏd — to say, speak (verb; ḏd in N "said by N", the formula that brings in a speech); ḏdt "words, speech" (noun from it) · a second word of the same spelling: the djed pillar, emblem of Osiris (noun m.; the pillar sign as a logogram) · also to be stable, enduring (verb; stative ḏd 'stable'; ꜥnḫ ḏd 'living and enduring')
glossary.snnw: snnw — second (ordinal numeral, from sn 'two'; sp snnw 'a second time')
glossary.dwꜣ: dwꜣ — to adore, praise, worship (verb; of a god) · also dwꜣw, adoration, praise (noun from it)
glossary.rꜥ: rꜥ — Ra, the sun-god (god's name; Budge: Rā) · also the sun; day (noun; rꜥ nb 'every day')
glossary.ḫft: ḫft — in front of, facing; in accordance with; at the time of, when (preposition; also before a verb form)
glossary.iꜣbtt: iꜣbtt — the east, the eastern quarter where the sun rises (noun f.) · also eastern (nisba adjective, feminine, after a feminine noun: ꜣḫt iꜣbtt 'the eastern horizon') · plural nisba iꜣbtyw, 'those of the east'
glossary.ḫt: ḫt — thing, things, property (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: wood, tree, stick, a wooden board (noun m.) · a third word: stairway, terrace (?) (noun; written with the stairway sign; Budge: χet, 'steps') · a fourth word: rear, following (noun; m-ḫt 'after', imyw-ḫt 'those in the following of') · a fifth word: fire, flame (noun; written with the flame as classifier; Budge: χet) · also a rod as a measure of length (?) (noun; Budge: χet)
glossary.i: i — O!, hail (the vocative interjection that opens each declaration)
glossary.ꜣny: ꜣny — Ani, royal scribe of Thebes, for whom the papyrus was made (personal name)
glossary.itn: itn — the disk of the sun, the Aten (noun)
glossary.pwy: pwy — this, that (masculine demonstrative, after its noun; hrw pwy 'that day')
glossary.stwt: stwt — rays, beams of light, esp. of the sun (noun f. plural; Budge: satetu) · a second word of the same spelling: meaning uncertain (?), written with a mummy-shaped classifier of images, perhaps from twt 'image' (noun) · also to shine, send out rays (?) (verb, spelled like the noun stwt)
glossary.hrw: hrw — terror, dread · a second word of the same spelling: day (noun; plural hrww)
glossary.psḏ: psḏ — to shine, appear in light (verb)
glossary.tw: tw — you (2nd person masculine singular dependent pronoun; object of a verb, or subject after mk) · also written ṯw, the older form of the same pronoun
glossary.dwꜣyt: dwꜣyt — dawn, morning (noun f.; written with the star dwꜣ; Budge: ṭuait)
glossary.sḥtp: sḥtp — to make content, satisfy, appease (verb; causative of ḥtp 'be content')
glossary.pri: pri — to go out, come forth (verb)
glossary.wḏꜣ: wḏꜣ — to proceed, go on, set out (verb) · a second word of the same spelling: to be sound, prosper (verb; ꜥnḫ wḏꜣ snb 'life, prosperity, health') · also the noun 'soundness, well-being' (noun m.)
glossary.mꜥnḏt: mꜥnḏt — the Mandjet-bark, the sun's bark of the morning (boat name; Budge: Māāṭet)
glossary.mni: mni — to moor, to come to land; of the dead, to end the voyage of life (verb)
glossary.sktt: sktt — Sektet, the evening bark of the sun (boat name; Budge: sektet)
glossary.ꜣbḫ: ꜣbḫ — to mix, mingle, join with (verb; Budge: àbeχ)
glossary.iḫmw-wrd: iḫmw-wrd — 'those who do not know weariness', the Unwearying Stars, the stars that never cease moving (plural noun, from ḫm 'not know' and wrd 'be weary'; Budge: àuχemu urṭu)
glossary.·ti: ·ti — you (2nd person singular ending of the stative: "you are …, you have …"; written ·tw here) · also written ·ṯi, with the tethering rope ṯ and the reed (the older spelling) · also 3rd person feminine singular ending of the stative: 'she, it is …' (written ·ṯi, as in sšw·ṯi 'it is emptied') · the 3rd feminine singular ending also written ·tw (rs·ti 'she is awake') · also for a 3rd person masculine subject (?) (a later use of the ending, or a slip)
glossary.swꜣš: swꜣš — to extol, praise (causative verb; Budge: suaś)
glossary.ḫpri: ḫpri — Khepri, 'he who comes into being', the sun-god at dawn, shown as a scarab (god's name; from ḫpr 'come into being'; Budge: χeperà)
glossary.ḫpr: ḫpr — to come into being, happen, become (verb)
glossary.ḏs: ḏs — self (noun; with a suffix, ḏs·f 'himself, by himself, of his own accord')
glossary.nfr: nfr — beautiful, good, perfect (adjective; follows its noun; verb 'be good'); also beauty, goodness (noun m.)
glossary.wy: wy — how …! (admirative particle after a verb or adjective; iy wy 'welcome!') · a second word of the same spelling: a word for a body of water, written with water, pool and canal classifiers (noun; reading and sense uncertain; Budge: ui 'lake')
glossary.sḥḏ: sḥḏ — to make bright, illuminate (causative verb; from ḥḏ 'be bright')
glossary.·sn: ·sn — they, them, their (3rd person plural suffix pronoun)
glossary.nbt-wnwt: nbt-wnwt — the Lady of the Hour, a goddess (goddess's name; from nbt 'lady' and wnwt 'hour'; Budge: Nebt-Unnut)
glossary.šmꜥ: šmꜥ — the South, Upper Egypt (noun m.; Budge: qemāu, his old value for the sign) · plural nisba šmꜥyw, 'those of the south' · also šmꜥt, 'the southern one', the cobra-goddess or crown of the South (feminine nisba used as a noun; with mḥtt 'the northern one')
glossary.mḥtt: mḥtt — north (noun); northern (nisba adjective, feminine) · also mḥty, the masculine 'northern' (nisba adjective) · plural nisba mḥtyw, 'those of the north'
glossary.wpt: wpt — brow, forehead; top of the head (noun f.; written with the horns; Budge: àpt)
glossary.iw: iw — opens a statement, often with a suffix (iw·f "he …"); not translated (particle)
glossary.sḏm·n·f: sḏm·n·f — the n of the sḏm·n·f, marking a completed action ("I have …", "I …ed") (verb form; written between the verb and its suffix)
glossary.ḥꜣt: ḥꜣt — front, forepart, the prow of a boat; beginning (noun f.)
glossary.ḏḥwty: ḏḥwty — Thoth, the ibis god of writing, reckoning and wisdom, recorder of the judgement of the dead (god's name; Budge: Teḥuti)
glossary.sswn: sswn — to destroy, punish (verb; Budge: sesunneṭ)
glossary.dwꜣt: dwꜣt — the Duat, the underworld through which the sun and the dead pass by night (noun f.; place name; Budge: Ṭuat)
glossary.sšm: sšm — image, figure (noun) · also procedure, the way a thing is done · also to lead, guide (verb); guide, leader (participle used as a noun)
glossary.ii: ii — to come (verb; ii·n·i "I have come")
glossary.ḫr: ḫr — to fall (verb) · a second word of the same spelling: to, near, with (preposition; of persons) · also 'before' (ḫr nṯrw 'before the gods') · a third word: the particle ḫr, which brings in a further case or a consequence (?) (particle; sometimes written ẖr) · also 'from' (of persons: ḫr s nty·f ḫr·f 'from the man with whom it is')
glossary.ḫnr: ḫnr — to restrain, hold back, shut in (verb)
glossary.sḏm·tw·f: sḏm·tw·f — the tw of the sḏm·tw·f, the passive or impersonal form ("one …", "… is done") (verb form; written after the verb, before its suffix)
glossary.šnꜥ: šnꜥ — to turn back, repel, hold back (verb 3-lit; šnꜥ·tw 'one is turned back')
glossary.mꜣwi: mꜣwi — to be new, be renewed (verb; Budge: maiu)
glossary.dgi: dgi — to look, look at, behold (verb; also written dgg)
glossary.nfrw: nfrw — beauty, goodness (noun; abstract plural of nfr "good, beautiful")
glossary.mi: mi — come! (the imperative that serves the verbs of coming, iwi and ii; in later copies written with the owl m and the forearm ꜥ, as if mꜥ, with the walking legs) · a second word of the same spelling: like, as (preposition)
glossary.ḥsi: ḥsi — to praise, favour (verb 3ae-inf.); ḥsy 'favoured one' (passive participle used as a noun; plural ḥsyw)
glossary.nty: nty — who, which, that (relative adjective); as a noun "he who" · also ntt 'that' (conjunction, after a preposition: ḥr ntt 'because')
glossary.nn: nn — not, there is not (negative particle; nn + noun 'there is no …'; nn + sḏm·f 'will not …', the negative of the future; nn with a sentence without a verb 'there is not, … is not') · a second word of the same spelling: these, those (demonstrative pronoun before its noun, in classical Egyptian joined to it by the genitive n, nn n X; in later texts also without it) · the demonstrative also written nnw; perhaps also standing first in a sentence without a verb, 'this is …' (?)
glossary.šps: šps — noble, august, venerable (adjective; follows its noun) · also rich, precious; a noble (noun) · also to be noble; with an object, to make noble, honour (?) (verb)
glossary.pḥ: pḥ — to reach, arrive at, attain (verb)
glossary.is: is — tomb (noun m.; Budge: àsi) · a second word of the same spelling: indeed (particle that stresses what precedes; ink is 'I am indeed')
glossary.wḏ: wḏ — to command, decree, ordain (verb) · also wḏt 'command, decree' (noun f., from the verb) · also wḏ 'command, decree' (noun m.)
